_what: The 'what we want' library — past reference creatives, organized by TYPE so any generation can pull real examples as targets and @Image references. Each source maps a FOLDER of examples to a (type, subtype, brand); examples.mjs resolves the actual files at query time, so this stays accurate as assets grow. Add a source whenever a new set of good reference work lands.

gold.why: The house single-take UGC talking-head lane exemplar: 30s, one unbroken shot, 9:16, no captions/logo — matches the measured house UGC laws (single-take, face-fills-frame, no-on-screen-text).
Approved-avatar (Sol) UGC with the Golden Hour card held beside the cheek — demonstrates the product-in-hand-without-covering-face framing law and the 5s rung of the duration ladder.
A clean Sol selfie talking-head take — the reusable-avatar UGC anchor showing native lip-sync / talking-face-not-hands discipline; the warm frame to start the next video from.

gold.type: Static ad creative (paid social / Meta a
gold.why: The corpus's strongest true conversion static: one dominant offer ('WIN $25,000 CASH + DODGE CHALLENGER'), unambiguous top-to-bottom hierarchy (headline -> logo -> hero car -> cash pile), high luminance/colour contrast on a dark ground, and cleanly gpt-image-2-rendered display type. Caveat: shipped at 3:4 (2160x2880), not the 4:5 feed optimum, and text fills the top ~40% (above the ~1/3 guideline).

gold.type: Static ad creative (paid social / Meta a
gold.why: Best product-forward static at the CORRECT feed ratio (4:5): single focal point, strong caustic-light contrast separating the vial from a deep-purple ground, brand colours and label legible. Exemplifies the hero/benefit-stack (retargeting) end of the spectrum. Caveat: no hook, offer, or CTA — it is a scene-hero, not a full cold-traffic ad; the side-label fine print garbles.

Best-in-class exemplar: exact hero prize ('$25,000+ AND DODGE CHALLENGER') shown as photoreal car + cash, the program-name/verification cluster ('MUHA MEMBERS RAFFLE' + faithful MM lockup + 5-star row + 'OFFICIAL ENTRY' badge), and a single CTA ('LEARN MORE'). It carries prize + legitimacy + action in three clean tiers — the full pattern minus a visible deadline.

Strong prize-hero exemplar: 'WIN $25,000 CASH + DODGE CHALLENGER' as the dominant element over a photoreal red Challenger + money stacks, with the brand monogram. Good stopping power and specificity, but instructively INCOMPLETE — no entry mechanic, no CTA, no disclosure/deadline — so it doubles as the 'poster not an ad' teaching case.

The brand asset folder holds the raffle-card fronts/backs and group-truck giveaway variants (incl. the QR raffle-back carrying 'Scan In Members App. To Redeem 10 Entries!' and 'No Purchase Necessary'), the repo's only real cluster of promo/giveaway entry-mechanic and disclosure work referenced in Muha_Meds.md.

Best in-repo example of the cinematic-ad LOOK for this type: caustic-lit hero frame, saturated high-contrast grade, 9:16 paid-social ratio. It is a still (a spot frame), not a finished multi-shot video, but it exemplifies the grade and hero-shot register the campaign lane should deliver.

Same cinematic-ad grade in the 4:5 campaign ratio (the ratio the house campaign/announce lane ships in, per house:ugc-ships-9x16-only which reserves 4:5 for the campaign/b-roll lane). Demonstrates the atmospheric, high-production product-hero beauty shot.
A real campaign/announce creative (not UGC) — closest brand-video-lane still in the corpus, showing multi-subject staged composition and brand-locked framing rather than a single-take selfie.

Best e-commerce-packshot exemplar in the corpus: ~30 SKUs on pure white with locked framing, scale, height and soft top-key lighting; color-coded caps are the only variable, powder is visible inside, brand+variant+dose legible. Textbook catalog consistency.

Single-SKU version of the same discipline with visible lavender powder — clean white ground, on-axis, legible NuLumin lockup and dose, soft contact reflection. Good reference for one product filling the frame correctly.
The 66-SKU white-background vial library — the scaled proof of cross-SKU consistency and the resolver's canonical packshot source; strong catalog-grid read.

Best floating-can packshot: 3/4 turn, clean white ground, soft gradient body reflection, bold legible DIALED lockup. Doubles as the canonical LEGIBILITY-FAILURE reference — truncated 'YOUR FULL POTE…' and garbled ingredient lines show the small-type melt to avoid.

The corpus's attempt at a hero lane — vials on colored ground strips with reflection. Useful as a reference for what is NOT yet a true hero (it is a white-BG packshot on a color chip, lacking directional key, gradient sweep and negative-fill edge definition), i.e. it marks the gap more than it fills it.
